title: The capital and financial account
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:33Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest point, e-bop, covers only the current account, so the capital and financial account and how it offsets a current account deficit is a separate idea that needs its own point.

draft.title: The capital and financial account
card: The capital and financial account records flows of investment and lending between Australia and the rest of the world. It covers the buying and selling of assets, such as shares, property and businesses, and borrowing and lending.
money coming into Australia from abroad, such as a foreign company buying an Australian business or a foreign bank lending to an Australian bank. It is a credit, so it adds to the account.
money going out of Australia, such as an Australian super fund buying shares overseas. It is a debit, so it subtracts from the account.

The balance of payments must add up to zero overall. So a current account deficit is matched by a surplus on the capital and financial account, because the money to pay for the deficit comes in as foreign investment and lending.
draft.remember: A current account deficit is paid for by net inflows of foreign investment and lending.

a.q: Which transaction is recorded in the capital and financial account?
opts: A Japanese firm buys a mine in Western Australia
An Australian pays for a holiday in Italy
Australia pays interest to a US bondholder
a.why: Buying a mine is a purchase of an Australian asset by a foreign investor, which is an investment flow. Wheat sales and holiday spending are trade in goods and services, and interest payments are an income flow. Those three belong to the current account.
a.clue: Look for the option where an asset changes owners.

b.q: Australia has a current account deficit this year. What does this mean for its capital and financial account?
opts: It shows a surplus, as foreign funds flow in
It shows a deficit of the same size
It shows a surplus, as Australia invests abroad
It shows a balance of zero
b.why: The balance of payments adds up to zero, so the deficit on the current account is matched by a surplus on the capital and financial account. That surplus is a net inflow of foreign investment and lending. A matching deficit would leave the total below zero, and investing abroad would be an outflow.
b.clue: Money to pay for the deficit has to come from somewhere.

a.best: A Japanese firm buys a mine in Western Australia

b.best: It shows a surplus, as foreign funds flow in
